newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-WAQAR TAKES HAT-TRICK ON WAY TO BEST CAREER HAUL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAQAR TAKES HAT-TRICK ON WAY TO BEST CAREER HAUL.

text.p: Pakistan test bowler Waqar Younis claimed a hat-trick on his way to a career-best haul of seven for 25 as Glamorgan routed Lancashire in the county championship on Saturday.
The game at Liverpool appeared to be heading for a certain draw after rain allowed only 50 overs on the first three days and then prevented any play before lunch on Saturday.
But captains Matthew Maynard and Neil Fairbrother agreed a Lancashire run chase of 273 in 60 overs and the Welsh county needed just 14 overs to roll over their hosts for 51.
Maynard said: "It was an amazing spell of bowling. The ball was swinging for Waqar and there wasn't much the Lancashire batsmen could do."
It was also a great day for Durham who recorded their first championship win for 24 matches when they beat championship leaders Kent by 135 runs at Darlington.
Superb seam and swing bowling from Simon Brown (four for 57) and Melvyn Betts (two for 25) ended Kent's stay at the top of the table.
Only 5.4 overs of the match remained when Durham captain David Boon, bowling his off-spin because of poor light, had Martin McCague caught at silly mid-off to end Kent's second innings on 132.
Middlesex are the new championship leaders following their 44-run win over Gloucestershire at Bristol.
